AE+SE from Redwood to provide benchmark artifacts and schedule hands-on test.
topics: Current stack & inference patterns (streaming vs non-streaming)
p95 latency SLOs and concurrency targets (tokens/sec expectations)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs: cost, isolation, predictable throughput

Security/compliance: SOC2, SAML, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-03 10:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Venturi CTO), Lina Gomez (Head of ML), Owen Price (Infra)
Links shared: Redwood benchmark spreadsheet (redwood.com/benchmarks/venturi-sample), SOC2 pack (link), SAML integration guide (link)

[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:10] Samir (Venturi): Samir here, CTO. Lina runs ML, Owen infra. Short on time so, we mainly want to understand latency at p95 for streaming responses and throughput for concurrent users — token per second stuff.
[00:24] Ava: Great; Diego from our SE team will own the deep perf stuff. Diego, real quick?
[00:30] Diego (Redwood SE): Hi all. We'll walk through what we need to reproduce your workload, and I'll propose a lightweight benchmark script that runs on your infra or ours. Typical artifacts: prompt set, concurrency profile, and target p95 SLOs.
[00:45] Lina (Venturi): For context, our chat assistants stream partial tokens to user as they type; p95 must be under 450ms for short prompts (~64 tokens), and for long-form generation we care about p95 <= 1.2s for 512-token responses. Also need to sustain 800 concurrent users during peak — each with streaming.
[01:05] Diego: Good detail. A few clarifying q's: are those p95s measured from request arrival to first token or to final token? And what's your tokenization?
[01:15] Samir: First token latency is our primary user-facing metric. We also track tail for final token but first token p95 is critical. We use tiktoken-ish BPE, so token counts similar to open models.
[01:30] Owen: Infrastructure: currently on AWS, K8s with node pools of A10G GPUs for batch jobs; inference is mostly on CPU autoscaled endpoints for lighter models. We want to move heavy ones to GPUs or Redwood Dedicated.
[01:46] Ava: Perfect. On hosting options: Redwood Hosted is quickest to start but shared capacity; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools & predictable throughput and Private gives full VPC/on-prem. For your p95 targets and 800 concurrency with streaming, Dedicated or Private likely the best fit.
[02:05] Lina: Cost is a consideration — we prefer predictable throughput vs pay per token. How much headroom do Dedicated nodes give?
[02:16] Diego: Depends on model size, quantization, and batch strategy. Quick example: with a 13B model quantized to 4-bit on an A100-style GPU, we typically see ~6-9 tokens/sec single-stream generation at low latency; with batching and streaming optimized runtime, aggregate tokens/sec scales near linearly up to GPU memory/bandwidth limits. For p95 first-token under 450ms at 64 tokens, Dedicated with proper batching + prefix cache can meet that for 100s of concurrent streams per GPU.
[02:47] Samir: When you say prefix cache, do you mean the KV cache for cached prefixes? We care about repeated context across users.
[02:56] Diego: Yes, KV cache/prefix caching — we do automatic cache hits for common prefixes and reuse KV to avoid recomputing early layers. Note: transcription sometimes shows K-V cash in my notes, sorry.
[03:10] Owen: How do streaming tokens/sec benchmarks run? We need a test that produces streaming partials at the same cadence as prod.
[03:18] Diego: We'll provide a token/sec benchmark harness that spawns X concurrent streams, drives prompt lengths and sampling parameters, and measures first-token latency, inter-token latency, and final token latency. We'll include both greedy and sampling tests.
[03:33] Lina: Is the benchmark safe to run on our VPC? We can't open things to public endpoints.
[03:38] Ava: For Private/Dedicated we'll run within your VPC or on-prem image; for Hosted we can run via secure temporary keys, or you can run the script locally and upload results.
[03:50] Samir: We need to ensure encryption/KMS and audit logs are intact if we give data. SOC2 compliance is a requirement.
[03:58] Diego: Redwood supports KMS integrations and has audit logs; we'll share SOC2 pack and SAML guide. The benchmark can be run against anonymized prompts if you want.
[04:10] Owen: Back to performance, what's your approach to quantization and kernel selection? We have a mixed fleet of models 7B->70B.
[04:22] Diego: Runtime picks kernels based on model arch and seq length; quantization profiles we recommend per-model and per-workload. For 7–13B, 4-bit gives big throughput gains with minimal quality regression for chat. For >30B we often recommend mixed precision or dedicated higher-end GPUs. We'll include model-specific guidance in the benchmark sheet.
[04:44] Lina: For 512-token responses, are we likely to hit your 1.2s p95? That seems tight for long outputs.
[04:52] Diego: For 512 tokens, 1.2s p95 for final token is unlikely; for first token it's feasible if model warm and KV hits. Are you measuring final token or streaming steady-state?
[05:05] Samir: Our KPI is first token p95 for response start; final tail we accept higher. Good to clarify.
[05:12] Diego: Then 1.2s first-token for 512 might be achievable with a dedicated pool and aggressive batching and prefix caching, but we should run the benchmark with your real prompts to be sure.
[05:25] Ava: Also, routing policies can send short low-latency queries to hosted or cheaper variants and heavy long-generation to dedicated/private to control cost.
[05:36] Owen: Speaking of routing, do you support automatic fallback when capacity constrained? We can't have degraded UX.
[05:43] Diego: Yes, smart routing with fallback to compatible model variants, and configurable SLO-based routing. We'll demo that in a follow-up.
[05:52] Lina: Any typical numbers you can share for p95 at different concurrencies? Even ballpark helps.
[05:58] Diego: Ballpark: single GPU with optimized runtime and 13B quantized might handle ~150–250 concurrent interactive streams (64-token type workloads) with first-token p95 ~300–500ms depending on sampling. Aggregate token/sec for that GPU in steady-state could be several thousand tokens/sec; the spreadsheet has sample rows.
[06:20] Samir: Our expected peak is 800 concurrent streams; if each GPU can do 200, we need ~4 GPUs reserved plus headroom — is that safe?
[06:28] Diego: That seems reasonable as a starting estimate, but end-to-end network, k8s overlay, and your infra specifics matter. We'll run the benchmark to adjust.
[06:38] Owen: We also use internal caching layer on top of model caching; what interactions should we be aware of?
[06:44] Diego: Great — top-layer cache is complementary. Redwood's prefix/KV caching operates at runtime; if your cache frequently hits, your model requests may be much cheaper. We'll want sample hit-rate numbers.
[06:55] Lina: On experiments: can we do an A/B where half traffic goes to Hosted and half to Dedicated to measure UX and cost delta?
[07:03] Ava: Yes, we support canary/A-B rollouts and tracing hooks in the console for per-route metrics.
[07:10] Samir: Security item — SAML & SSO integration timeline? We need SSO before we can give broader team access.
[07:17] Ava: We can share a SAML guide; setting up SSO for RBAC usually takes a week-ish depending on your IdP. We'll include it in the pack.
[07:25] Owen: About data retention — do hosted logs keep raw request text? We can't have PII in long-term logs.
[07:32] Diego: By default we keep minimal request metadata; for Hosted customers we can enable controls or recommend Dedicated/Private if you need no persistent request logging. KMS and customer-managed keys available for Private.
[07:46] Lina: Cool. If we do Dedicated, what's the procurement lead time? 
[07:51] Ava: Reserved Dedicated pools typically require a few weeks to provision depending on region and GPU availability; we can fast-track but procurement & contract sign-off adds time.
[07:59] Samir: Good to know. For the benchmark, what exact artifacts do you need from us?
[08:04] Diego: Sample prompt set, intended concurrency profile (ramp up pattern), target p95 SLOs, sample tokenization or tokenizer config, and any privacy constraints (e.g., anonymize prompts). Also your preferred model family/size.
[08:18] Samir: We'll share those — Lina will own the prompt set, Owen infra will share k8s access details if we run in VPC.
[08:26] Ava: Next step Ill email pricing and the spreadsheet; Diego will drop the benchmark harness. Can we pencil in a benchmarking session next week?
[08:34] Lina: Yes, Tue or Wed works.
[08:36] Owen: Tue afternoon preferred.
[08:38] Diego: I'll block Tue 2pm PT as tentative and share the runbook.
[08:42] Ava: Quick question from my side — do you have internal thresholds where Dedicated procurement kicks off? e.g., spend / concurrency?
[08:49] Samir: If monthly projected peak compute exceeds our cloud budget for model inference more than 30% over current, we escalate. But roughly once we expect sustained 500 concurrent interactions we start procurement conversations.
[09:03] Diego: That helps. We'll model cost vs latency tradeoffs in the shared spreadsheet so you can make that call.
[09:10] Lina: Anything else on security? Audits?
[09:14] Ava: We'll attach SOC2 and our security questionnaire. If you need penetration test reports we can surface them via our security team.
[09:23] Samir: Good. Last technical: what about tokenization differences and how you measure tokens/sec across model backends?
[09:30] Diego: We normalize to GPT-style tokens for bench comparability and include a tokenizer mapping step. The benchmark reports tokens/sec, first-token p95, inter-token latency distributions, and aggregate GPU tokens/sec metrics.
[09:46] Lina: Also include streaming artifact breakdown: network serialization overhead, inference compute, and post-processing.
[09:53] Diego: Will do. We'll also record per-route latency in our tracing.
[10:00] Ava: Anything else from Venturi?
[10:03] Owen: No, just please make sure the harness supports sampling top-k/top-p which we use heavily.
[10:08] Diego: Included.
[10:11] Samir: Thanks, appreciate the quick run-through.
[10:14] Ava: Recap of next steps — I'll send pricing/bench sheet & SOC2; Diego will share harness and tentative Tue 2pm PT slot; Venturi will share prompts and SLOs.
[10:27] Lina: Sounds good.
[10:30] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the CRM with docs and calendar invite.

End of transcript.
